official_measurement_examples.name: Consent threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: Hazardous substances consent is required where controlled hazardous substances are present at or above applicable legal thresholds, subject to statutory rules and exemptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: HSA decision role
official_measurement_examples.fact: The hazardous substances authority, usually the local planning authority, determines consent applications; HSE is a statutory consultee rather than the consenting authority.

official_measurement_examples.name: Three consultation zones
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE commonly sets inner, middle and outer consultation zones around major hazard sites using risk assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Web App advice
official_measurement_examples.fact: The HSE Planning Advice Web App can return Advises Against or Does Not Advise Against on safety grounds, which the planning authority must take into account rather than treat as the whole planning decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: Development sensitivity
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE advice depends on consultation zone plus development type, scale and sensitivity rather than proximity alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Hazardous substances consent does not override a separate need for planning permission or environmental permits.

official_measurement_examples.name: Consultation distance
official_measurement_examples.fact: A site lying inside an HSE consultation distance triggers consultation logic but does not by itself establish that development must be refused.

official_measurement_examples.name: Pipeline/site distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Major hazard installations and major accident hazard pipelines use related but distinct consultation-zone assessments and must not be merged into one generic buffer.

core_rules: hazardous substances consent is not planning permission
planning permission is not hazardous substances consent
HSE consultation distance is not automatic refusal
inner middle outer zones are risk-advice zones not ownership boundaries
HSE advice is not the hazardous substances authority decision
HSE advises-against is a material safety input not the whole planning decision
development sensitivity and scale must be retained
major hazard site and pipeline zones must not be merged
controlled quantity tests must not be guessed from proximity
COMAH regulation is distinct from land-use planning consent
historic consultation zones must retain current consent basis
hazard geometry does not determine land ownership or access
hazard consultation does not reserve development capacity
no parcel hazardous-substance clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
